tasks.spec:
You are an Elixir engineer fixing two small, independent bugs. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the Cornerman repo, an Elixir/OTP port of the Python agent-swarm tool Ringer. Cornerman must behave exactly like the pinned Python Ringer (the oracle, run on Python 3.12.13). Edit files here directly.

NEVER TOUCH: anything under test/ (the tests are the acceptance check), DIVERGENCES.toml, bin/, mix.exs, mix.lock, .git, vendor/, and every file under lib/ except the owned ones below. In particular do NOT edit lib/cornerman/manifest.ex or lib/cornerman/app_config.ex: they call the functions you fix and are correct. Do not git commit, push or git add. Do not add dependencies.

OWNED PATHS (the only files you may create or edit): lib/cornerman/py.ex, lib/cornerman/py/pwd.ex, lib/cornerman/py/text.ex (only if a helper genuinely belongs there) and ./notes.md.

BUG 1, lib/cornerman/py.ex, `Cornerman.Py.resolve/1`. It emulates Python's `Path(text).expanduser().resolve()`, lexically: symlinks are never followed, and that is intended (the difference it causes is recorded in DIVERGENCES.toml; keep it). Its return value is right and must not change: the lexical absolute path (`Path.expand` after `expanduser`). What is wrong is the error for a path holding a lone surrogate (a code point U+D800..U+DFFF, which Cornerman carries as its three-byte generalised UTF-8 form; see lib/cornerman/py/text.ex, `Text.encode_error/1`). Python raises `UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode character '\ud800' in position N: surrogates not allowed` from inside `os.path.realpath`, and N is counted in the path realpath is about to lstat when it first meets the surrogate, NOT in the absolute path. Read `_joinrealpath` in /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/lib/python3.12/posixpath.py. It walks the components of the path in order, starting from "" for a relative path and "/" for an absolute one: empty components and "." are skipped; ".." pops the last component of the path built so far (or, when that path is empty or already ends in "..", appends ".."); every other component is joined on and the result is lstat-ed, and that lstat is what raises. So a relative path stays relative (the current directory is never prepended), and a surrogate in a component that a later ".." would remove still raises, because it is lstat-ed before the ".." is seen. Today Cornerman expands to the absolute path first and counts there, so relative paths get the wrong position. Only the position (and whether an error happens at all) changes; the message format stays exactly as Text.encode_error builds it.

Truth table from the oracle (cwd is irrelevant for relative paths, that is the point): workdir "w\ud800" -> position 1; "sub/dir/w\ud800" -> 9; "../w\ud800" -> 4; "./x/../w\ud800" -> 1; "../../x/../../w\ud800" -> 10; repo "r\ud800" -> 1; absolute "/usr/../w\ud800" -> 2 (already right today). `~` and `~user` expansion happens before the walk, as now, so "~/w\ud800" counts in the expanded absolute path.

BUG 2, lib/cornerman/py/pwd.ex, `Cornerman.Py.Pwd.current_home/0`. It is used when HOME is unset, to emulate Python's `pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir`. Today it runs `id -un` and then looks the user up BY NAME, which is not what Python does: getpwuid looks the entry up BY UID, and the two differ whenever several accounts share a uid or the name lookup finds a different record. Change it to look up by uid: get the real uid with `/usr/bin/id -u` (Python's os.getuid() is the real uid), then on macOS `/usr/bin/dscacheutil -q user -a uid <uid>` and read its `dir: ` line; elsewhere `getent passwd <uid>` and take the line whose THIRD field equals the uid exactly (getent also answers numeric lookups for a name that happens to be digits, so match on the uid field, not the name field), falling back to reading /etc/passwd and matching the third field when getent is not installed. Keep `home_of/1` (the by-name lookup for `~user`) as it is. No shell: every argument travels as one argv element to System.cmd, as the module does now. Update the module's moduledoc and the function doc so they describe what the code does. `id -un` must not appear in the file afterwards.

THE TESTS: in test/conformance/lint_test.exs the cases lint/error-surrogate-relative-workdir, lint/error-surrogate-relative-workdir-subdir, lint/error-surrogate-relative-workdir-parent, lint/error-surrogate-relative-workdir-dot, lint/error-surrogate-relative-workdir-parents and lint/error-surrogate-relative-repo fail today and must pass (fixtures in test/conformance/fixtures/lint/). Every other case in that file passes today and must still pass, including lint/error-surrogate-position-symlinked-workdir (the ledgered symlink difference: it must keep differing only in the position) and the lint/home-unset/* cases, which run with HOME unset and exercise bug 2.

SETUP (run once, first, from this directory; the sandbox cannot fetch packages):
  cp -R /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/deps ./deps
  export PATH=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/elixir/1.20.1-otp-28/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/erlang/28.5/bin:$PATH HEX_OFFLINE=1 MIX_ENV=test CORNERMAN_ORACLE=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/.claude/worktrees/agent-abebfb31762ae2c5f/vendor/ringer-py CORNERMAN_PYTHON=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3

HOW TO RUN (after the setup, from this directory):
  mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format
  mix test test/conformance/lint_test.exs
To compare one manifest by hand: `RINGER_NO_SELF_UPDATE=1 /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3 /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/.claude/worktrees/agent-abebfb31762ae2c5f/vendor/ringer-py/ringer.py lint <manifest>` against `bin/cornerman lint <manifest>`, both run from the same directory.
Your sandbox may block writes outside this directory and a scratch dir; if a test cannot run there, say so in notes.md. The verifying check runs outside the sandbox and has 60 seconds: owned paths only, `mix format --check-formatted`, `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, no `id -un` in pwd.ex, and test/conformance/lint_test.exs green.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: the two fixes, formatted and compiling with no warnings, plus ./notes.md saying what you changed in each file and why, what you ran, and anything the sandbox stopped you from verifying.
tasks.verified: the six relative-path surrogate cases and the rest of the lint conformance file pass; Pwd.current_home no longer finds the user by name; only lib/cornerman/py.ex, lib/cornerman/py/pwd.ex, lib/cornerman/py/text.ex and notes.md changed.
